examples.text: Его паспорт и настоящую медицинскую книжку повара.

examples.text: Я медицинский работник.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'booklet / record' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Его паспорт и настоящую медицинскую книжку повара.

examples.text: Она читает детскую книжку.
examples.trans: She is reading a children's book.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'works', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Родион Сергеевич останется работать здесь!
examples.trans: Rodion Sergeyevich will stay here to work!

examples.text: Вот здесь можно сделать вторую летнюю веранду.

examples.trans: Yes, that is a fact, the place here is very cozy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втрашний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tomorrow's').

examples.text: Родион Сергеевич работает с завтрашнего дня, завтра и увидите!
examples.trans: Rodion Sergeyevich starts work tomorrow, so you will see them tomorrow!

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень завтрашний выбор.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'day' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я любитель остатков пищи этого чудного заведения.

examples.trans: Good afternoon, allow me to interrupt your quiet conversation.

examples.text: Уважаемый мужчина, вот вам деньги, только я умоляю.
examples.trans: Respected sir, here is money for you, only I beg you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Об этом вы завтра поговорите с полицией.
examples.trans: You will talk about that with the police tomorrow.

examples.text: Завтра здесь будут ужинать важные инвесторы с женой.

examples.text: Родион Сергеевич работает с завтрашнего дня, завтра и увидите!
examples.trans: Rodion Sergeyevich starts work tomorrow, so you will see them tomorrow!

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ставить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'imagine', paired with 'представлять'.

examples.text: Позвольте мне представиться, меня зовут Родион Сергеевич.
examples.trans: Allow me to introduce myself, my name is Rodion Sergeyevich.

examples.text: Позвольте представить: звезда и лицо нашего ресторана Дмитрий!
examples.trans: Allow me to introduce: the star and face of our restaurant, Dmitry!

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, можете себе представить, это моя жена!
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, can you imagine, this is my wife!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is testing', paired with 'проверить'.

examples.text: Костя, представь, Вика меня проверяет, как будто я террорист!
examples.trans: Kostya, imagine, Vika is testing me as if I were a terrorist!

examples.trans: He is testing us.

examples.text: Учитель проверяет тетради.
examples.trans: The teacher is checking notebooks.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if, though', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне кажется, здесь будет очень тихо и уютно.
examples.trans: It seems to me it will be very quiet and cozy here.

examples.text: В смысле, и что ты теперь будешь делать?
examples.trans: I mean, and what are you going to do now?

examples.text: Думаю, что скоро буду в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: I think that I will be at our restaurant soon.

meanings.note: Agent noun formed with the international suffix '-ист' denoting a specialist or adherent. Common masculine noun meaning 'terrorist' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Костя, представь, Вика меня проверяет, как будто я террорист!
examples.trans: Kostya, imagine, Vika is testing me as if I were a terrorist!

examples.text: Ну, в каком-то смысле ты тот ещё террорист.
examples.trans: Well, in a sense you really are quite the terrorist.

examples.text: А слепые — это террористы.
examples.trans: And the blind are terrorists.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Только этот, но вы, пожалуйста, не волнуйтесь.

examples.text: Зачем ты сейчас ей неправду по телефону сказал?

examples.trans: Do not worry, he is healthy, we got him his shots.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some, some kind of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, найдите себе какой-нибудь другой ресторан.

examples.trans: Yes, or if some handsome guy treats me.

examples.trans: What nonsense.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мысл'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sense, meaning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В смысле, и что ты теперь будешь делать?
examples.trans: I mean, and what are you going to do now?

examples.text: Ну, в каком-то смысле ты тот ещё террорист.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I mean, and what are you going to do now?

examples.text: Зачем ты сейчас ей неправду по телефону сказал?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nothing happened, I threw that phone number away immediately!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Зачем ты сейчас ей неправду по телефону сказал?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, Катя, а у тебя с Максом что-то есть?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.

examples.text: Ну что, успокоился?
examples.trans: Well, have you calmed down?

examples.trans: Calm down, please!

examples.trans: Calm down, everything's fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
